title: Learning Imbalanced Datasets with Label-Distribution-Aware Margin Loss
authors: Kaidi Cao, Colin Wei, Adrien Gaidon, Nikos Arechiga, Tengyu Ma
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2019), volume 32
conclusions: Derives a fine-grained, per-class generalization error bound showing balanced test error scales with 1/(gamma_j * sqrt(n_j)), motivating class-dependent margins rather than a single global margin

Proposes LDAM (Label-Distribution-Aware Margin) loss, a softmax cross-entropy variant that enforces class-dependent margins Delta_j proportional to n_j^{-1/4}, giving minority classes larger margins than frequent classes

Proposes a Deferred Re-balancing (DRW/DRS) training schedule: train with vanilla ERM first, then apply re-weighting/re-sampling only after annealing the learning rate, which outperforms re-weighting/re-sampling from the start

Shows LDAM and deferred re-balancing are complementary; combined (LDAM-DRW) beats ERM, focal loss, class-balanced (CB) re-weighting/re-sampling, and hinge-margin variants on imbalanced CIFAR-10/100 (long-tailed and step imbalance), imbalanced IMDB, Tiny ImageNet, and iNaturalist 2018
Also sketches an extension for the setting where the (imbalanced but non-uniform) test label distribution is known rather than assumed uniform
